utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. The Chamber apologies for the late start. We only have procedural issues today on my agenda. I have a few. The first one is the Chamber would like to hear from the Prosecution which will be the next witness to be examined when.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour, there may be -- I think there'll be a protective measures application filed today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's the reason I didn't mention the name I had on my mind. Could we turn into private session for a second.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then I think for two witnesses, the last one being Vesel Dizdari, 92 ter statement should be read into the record. Again, for the public, these summaries are read into the record, so that the public instead of having to consult the filed statements by just listening to these proceedings is approximately aware of what their evidence is about. Please proceed, Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, and good morning. This is the summary of 92 ter statement of Witness Vesel Dizdari. "The witness is an Albanian male who was born in the village of Kosuriq Kosovo, 1958."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney, I now already may ask your attention for the speed you developed within one or two lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: It's a bad habit, Your Honour. I'm sorry. "The witness currently resides and works in Kosovo with his family. The witness was previously employed in various positions outside of Kosovo, including as a cook in the Yugoslav Army in 1978 and 1979, a physical labourer in Slovenia, and a miner in Switzerland. "For a period during 1998, he lived with his family in Kosovo. During that period, he was not a formal member of the KLA, but he was involved in the protection of his village from the Serbs. During August of 1998, he was captured and briefly held by the Serbs before being released." "The witness states that there were KLA HQs in various locations near his home, including in Baran, Strellc, and Vranoc. The witness does not know who the individual commanders of these HQs were. The witness states that although the KLA had no prison in Baran, there was a school there used for military purposes. There was also a KLA presence in Kosuriq with soldiers everywhere. "The witness had a uniform with a KLA badge on the sleeve, but he did not have official KLA papers. The witness saw some villagers wearing black uniforms, but he did not have any real contact with them. He thought they were part of the military police. When the Serbs attacked -- when the Serb attack occurred in September of 1998, the witness left and went to Albania. "On a date before 7 September 1998, the witness was ordered by KLA Commander Mete Krasniqi to go to the home of Zenun Gashi in Kosuriq and to bring him to the school in Baran. The witness did this and handed Zenun Gashi over to Commander Mete Krasniqi. The witness also searched the home of Zenun Gashi on the orders of Mete Krasniqi. Subsequently, Mete Krasniqi told the witness to come and work for the military police. "The witness did not use physical force on Zenun Gashi, nor did he see anything being done to him by other soldiers. The witness did not know the reason for Zenun Gashi's arrest. The witness did not know of any other arrests. He heard his neighbour, Vuk Vukovic, was reported missing, but he did not know anything further about the incident. "The witness knew a shop owner named Sanije Balaj for five years before September of 1998. He saw her being arrested in September of 1998 in Baran Kosovo."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: "He saw her in the company of Commander Krasniqi, other KLA soldiers, and two of her relatives. The witness did not intervene in the conversation between Commander Krasniqi and Sanije Balaj and does not know what the conversation was about. Later, Sanije Balaj's brother asked the witness if he had seen his sister. The witness relayed that he had seen her in Baran. The witness later heard people say she had been murdered or went missing. "The witness knew nothing about bodies in Lake Radonjic, either during or after the war." Your Honour, that concludes the statement of Witness Vesel Dizdari. I do have one previous one for Witness 62, it's much shorter, that has not been read into the record at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you would do that now, that would be fine, and if you would keep the pace of the last few lines, Mr. Kearney, that would certainly assist both interpreters and the transcriber.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour. Thank you. This is a 92 ter summary for Witness 62. This witness testified on the 12th and 13th of June. "The witness is a Kosovar Albanian and lived with his wife and two children in his home village in Kosovo, until the August 1998 Serb offensive forced him to leave. His family was involved in a feud with another Kosovar Albanian family. The witness was convicted for crimes committed in the course of this feud and served six years in prison. "On 25 June 1998, the Serbian police abandoned the witness's area, and it fell under complete KLA control. Two Kosovar Albanians, whom the witness considered his family's enemies, became KLA commanders of his home village. "A few days before the abduction of the witness's parents, Rrustem Tetaj, dressed in a camouflage uniform bearing KLA insignia, accompanied by soldiers wearing black uniforms, visited the witness's family. He introduced himself as a deputy of Ramush Haradinaj and asked the family to refrain from any retaliatory action against the other family throughout the duration of the war in Kosovo. "Two days after Tetaj's visit, a Kosovar Albanian, travelling with the witness's parents on the road to Peje, was captured and held for a short time by Montenegrins. Subsequently, this person was arrested by Rrustem Tetaj and taken to Gllogjan headquarters, ostensibly because he was travelling without a movement pass." Your Honours, that is the conclusion of the second 92 ter summary. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kearney. Then the Chamber still has to deliver a decision on protective measures for Witness 63. This is the Trial Chamber's decision on the Prosecution's 11th motion for trial-related protective measures. On the 29th of May, 2007, the Prosecution applied for protective measures for a person whose statement has been introduced into evidence in accordance with Rule 92 bis. This statement has Exhibit Number P339. The Prosecution asked for the assignment of a pseudonym and that no identifying information of the witness should be disclosed to the public. The Defence has informed the Trial Chamber that it does not oppose the application. The Trial Chamber has set out the standard to be met for granting protective measures in numerous decisions, and there is no need to repeat it here. The witness has expressed fear for his safety, and that of his family, should it become publicly known that he has given evidence for the Prosecution. The witness lives in a small village in Kosovo, together with his family. Given the nature of the witness's testimony, the Trial Chamber is satisfied that it may antagonise persons who reside in his community. Therefore, as the Trial Chamber is satisfied that the requirements for granting protective measures are met, the Trial Chamber grants the Prosecution's request for pseudonym and that no identifying information of the witness is disclosed to the public. The witness will be assigned the pseudonym Witness 63, and the witness statement will be admitted under seal. The redacted witness statement attached to the Prosecution's 11th motion for trial-related protective measures will be admitted under the same exhibit number, P339, as the public and redacted version of the statement. This concludes the Trial Chamber's decision on the Prosecution's 11th motion for trial-related protective measures. I now move on to the next item; that is, two exhibits on which still a decision on admission has to be taken. The first one is P340, which is the testimony of Witness Jakup Krasniqi in the Limaj case, transcript pages 3285 up to and including 3493, with eight annexes attached. The Haradinaj Defence has already expressed that it has no objections against admission. Originally, there were nine exhibits attached, but one of them was a double for an exhibit that was already admitted. Just to be sure, is there any objection from the Balaj or --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: There is not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Brahimaj Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Nor from the Brahimaj Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then P340 is admitted into evidence. Another exhibit marked for identification, but no decision yet taken, is a hand-drawn map, P352. If I remind the parties that it's not easy to follow the geography on that map, where rivers seem to play an important role, then it may be clear to all parties which map we are talking about. Are there any objections against admission? I see nodding three times "no," therefore, P352 is admitted into evidence. I have no further matters on my agenda. The Chamber is waiting for an update to be filed, I take it later today, of the witness list. There is an informal request by the Defence where no clear answer yet exists, as far as the Prosecution is concerned, to have a meeting with lead counsel, not in court, to discuss some practical matters. There's no need at this moment, I think, to make any submissions on the matter. The Chamber has already indicated that it certainly will not take any steps, will not follow any suggestion until the moment that it has received the updated witness list. The Chamber will also consider what exactly the purpose of such a meeting should be, and therefore whether it should be held, yes or no. I noticed that the parties may have different expectations at this moment about it, but we'll wait and see and then further inform the parties. At the same time, I thought it good that it is on the record where sometimes, as I've explained earlier, sometimes informal communications do exist, that if they go beyond what is purely practical, that it should leave traces on the record so that the public knows what is going on. Is there any matter to be raised by the parties? Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I have another Rule 92 ter summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: For Mr. Cufe Krasniqi's evidence last week. Is it appropriate for me to read it now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is appropriate. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I know the interpreters and the transcribers have a copy, but I will listen to the French when I am speaking so I can keep up with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The French are now there. This is a summary of the Rule 92 ter testimony of Mr. Cufe Krasniqi, heard on the 14th and 15th of June, 2007, at pages 5703 to 5859 of the transcript. "Cufe Krasniqi, a Kosovar Albanian, born on the 24th of March, 1959, in Peje municipality, was a KLA commander based in Baran from about June 1998 on. He was a police officer in the Yugoslav police service until he was dismissed from it in 1990. He hid from the Serb authorities in the mountains of Hajle for about six years. "In 1993, the witness heard about the KLA for the first time. He joined the KLA in February 1998 at the request of Mete Krasniqi. The witness was responsible for training young KLA soldiers in Vranoc under the command of Din Krasniqi. To join the KLA, new recruits had to be accompanied by someone guaranteeing for their trust-worthiness. "By February 1998, it was well-known that Lahi Brahimaj commanded an army in Jablanica. Jablanica was the oldest KLA headquarter in western Kosovo because it was not easily accessible by the Serb forces. The KLA was also organised in Gllogjan, which became the most important KLA headquarters, after the attack on the Jashari compound in March 1998. "The attack in Gllogjan in March 1998 was the first public victory by the KLA. After this attack, the KLA started to operate openly. By March 1998, 40 to 50 villages in the Dukagjini area were under KLA control. Even after [sic] the Dukagjini Operational Zone was formally established, Ramush Haradinaj was regarded as the de facto commander of the area. The Serbian forces controlled the main road between Peje, Decan, and Gjakove, but did not dare to enter the villages. "From late March 1998 on, the Serbs were shelling the villages of the Dukagjini Zone from their artillery positions. In early May 1998, the Serbian police had retreated to the Irzniq police station from which they evacuated. In June 1998, the last police station in the Dukagjini Zone in Qallapek was evacuated. "The KLA structure at the village level consisted of a general commander, a deputy commander, an operations commander for training soldiers, a logistics commander, and the commander of the guards. "In May 1998, the witness met Idriz Balaj for the first time when he was driving in his black Jeep. A month later the witness learned about the Black Eagles that he considered a well-respected unit. "In June 1998, the FARK officers under command of Tahir Zemaj arrived in the Dukagjini Zone from Albania. The witness joined the Adrian Krasniqi Brigade in Baran under Rrustem Berisha, but it was de facto led by Nazif Ramabaja. In the same brigade were Musa Draga and Esat Ademaj. Sadri Selca was also another KLA member in Baran reporting to Nazif Ramabaja. "Ramush Haradinaj visited the brigade two or three times and took part in the oath-taking ceremony, together with Rrustem Tetaj, Nazif Ramabaja, Tahir Zemaj, and many others at the Baran school on the 20th of July, 1998. In June 1998, a military unit was formed in Baran school under the command of Hasan Gashi. The military police of the KLA enforced discipline in the KLA. "On 6th of June, 1998, the battle of Loxha took place." Can I just interpose. I think that was corrected in cross-examination to July 1998; however, it appears in his 92 ter statement as June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: "From about the 26th of August to the 6th of September, 1998, the Serbs overtook the area in a big offensive against the Albanians. In September 1998, Tahir Zemaj left Kosovo. After the fall of Gllogjan, Ramush Haradinaj was with the witness at Prapaqan. The witness later fled to Brolic and Jablanica."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEARNEY
utterances.text: Trial Chamber, may I have one moment with Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Kearney has just pointed out at page 9, line 2, if I could just check it. Oh, yes. Where the transcript says: "Even after the Dukagjini Operational Zone was formally established, Ramush Haradinaj was regarded as the de facto commander of the area." Either I read it incorrectly or it was transcribed incorrectly. The summary of the witness's testimony actually reads the following. I'll read the two lines. "By March 1998, 40 to 50 villages in the Dukagjini area were under KLA control. Even before the Dukagjini Operational Zone was formally established, Ramush Haradinaj was regarded as the de facto commander of the area."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I simple observe there were a number of aspects of the summary with which one might not necessarily agree, but the treating of the summary as being --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The summary is not -- it's just to inform the public. Now, I think it was good practice that the summaries would be presented to the Defence so they can make comments to contribute, so that the way in which the evidence is reflected and presented to the public is as precise as follow. Therefore, I don't know whether that took place or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It did, and I've taken the general view with the summaries provided, broadly speaking, reflect the 92 ter statement, then given they're not evidence in the case, I'm not intervening in relation to the content.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Only if it might mislead the public, which might not be the case if you could argue about some details. Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I really only saw this for the first time this morning, and I was a little troubled in paragraph 3 by the statement: "In February 1998, it was well-known that Lahi Brahimaj commanded an army in Jablanica," but I take that to be a reflection of the witness's testimony at 5846, 20, where he said that, "At this time, every village has its own staff, has its own army fighting against an army belonging a state." So I think the word "army" is used in an extremely loose sense at this particular juncture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand that you might have used other words to express the same, but the evidence is the statement and any additional testimony to that. And this is just to inform the public. It's now all put on the record. Any other procedural issues, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just don't have Mr. Krasniqi's statement in front of me, but my clear recollection is that the statement uses the word --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. When I said you would have just -- you would have used another word, I did not refer to the summary but to the word used by the witness and what he describes as a matter of fact. Let's not further argue on this. Any other further procedural issues on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Not from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not from the Defence. Then we adjourn to Thursday, the 21st of June, 9.00, Courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 21st day of June, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 9.55 a.m.,
